[MATCHES-ON-REVIEW, confidence high] THE FEAT LISTS ARE THE SAME SET, verified rather than eyeballed. I enumerated every record in public/core.json with level === 1, the `druid` trait, and an order in `prerequisites`: fire-lung [flame order], shore-step [wave order], steadying-stone [stone order], animal-companion [animal order], leshy-familiar [leaf order], storm-born [storm order], untamed-form [untamed order] — seven, and featPickGrants.ts:94 lists exactly those seven ids. Our fixed list and their dynamic filter resolve over the identical universe, so the pick offered is the same.
OUR EXTRA CHOICE IS NOT INERT — I checked before judging it (instrument lesson 1). `exploredOrder` is read through a sibling record: effect-backfill.json:67339 gives Order Magic `"limitToAnswersOf": "order-explorer"`, and build.ts:1595 consumes it as `const limitTo = def.limitToAnswersOf ? answersInOtherTakes(def.limitToAnswersOf, build) : null`. So Order Magic's option list is restricted to the orders you actually explored — which is precisely the printed "you are now a member of that order for the purpose of meeting feat prerequisites", the clause WG leave implicit. Removing this choice would silently break Order Magic.
The repeatability matches too: the record carries `maxTakable: null` for the printed "You can take this feat multiple times", and the Order Magic definition beside it carries `distinctAcrossTakes: true` for "you must choose a different order".
SO: different decomposition, same delivery. They ask one question (which feat) and infer the order; we ask two (which order, then which feat) because a second record needs the order answer by name.
MENU NOTE, ours to decide: `exploredOrder` offers 9 orders, but only 7 have a 1st-level order feat — cultivation-order and spore-order have none in our data (confirmed by the enumeration above), so picking either yields no feat from the printed clause. Narrowing that list is authorised menu filtering; it does not change any mechanical output, and both of those orders still deliver through Order Magic's initial order spell.

THE BASIC UNDEAD BENEFITS ARE THE DIFFERENT CARRIER, and they line up one-to-one. WG deliver them implicitly through `giveTrait` undead; we enumerate them as fields. I read the printed source (C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/rules/rules-1694.json, "Basic Undead Benefits", Book of the Dead pg. 44) and mapped every bullet: **Necril** → `grantsLanguages: ['necril']`; **Undead Vision** ("low-light vision, or darkvision if your ancestry already has low-light vision") → `conditionalSenses: [{ ifPresent:'low-light-vision', base:{name:'low-light-vision'}, upgraded:{name:'darkvision'} }]`, which is the conditional shape the sentence actually requires; **Negative Healing** → `negativeHealing: true`; **Negative Survival** → the record's `note`, which paraphrases the bullet accurately (knocked out and dying at 0 HP, stabilize does not benefit you, destroyed rather than dead); **Immunity to Death Effects** → `immunities: ['death effects']`. Our `situational` +1 circumstance against disease and poison is the remaining benefit from the same sidebar. Nothing in that list is missing and nothing is invented.
The record's `dataWarning` already discloses the one genuinely absent piece — the Revulsion and Sunlight vulnerabilities, whose sidebar text is not in the mirror — so the gap is surfaced to the player rather than silently dropped. WG encode no vulnerability ops either, so this is not a divergence between us.
Every field above is carried in scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, so it survives `npm run data`.

Their side grants the base light+medium, then expert (and a master step) in those categories once the character's class reaches expert armour. Ours had the base grants frozen at trained forever: the feat's second printed sentence — 'Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor, you also gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat' — had no carrier at all, so a 13th-level fighter wore medium armour at trained while their class had made them a master of it. Built `FeatGrant.armorMirrorBest`, the armour twin of weaponFamiliarity.mirrorBestCategory, applied after class advancement for the same reason. It raises only categories the feat actually granted (a wizard whose conditional never gave heavy does not get it) and never reads UNARMORED, which the sibling clause excludes in parentheses. 4 tests.

FIXED. 'You gain the tactics class feature like a commander and gain your own folio; this folio contains two common mobility or offensive tactics of your choosing. You can prepare one of these tactics whenever a commander would be able to prepare tactics.' The whole subsystem was gated on ownsClass('commander'), which a dedication never satisfies — an archetype commander picked no tactics, stored none, saw none, and the only carrier was a note apologising that archetype tactics aren't tracked. Their row (45508) opens with TWO 'Select a Tactic' pickers filtered {traits:['Tactic'], level:{max:1}}, which is our tacticTier 'basic'. Built on the runesmith-via-dedication template: the two capacities live on the record that prints them (folioTactics 2, preparedTactics 1) and are read through tableMax, never restated in code — the class's own 5 and 3 would have given a dedicated character a folio nearly three times the size the feat grants. Tier is basic and does not follow the class ladder, rising to expert only on a SECOND Tactical Excellence at 8th, which that feat prints. Tactical Expansion and Tactical Excellence already carried commander-folio counter mods that had fired for nobody and now apply. THE 'UNSETTLED NUMBER' IN THE FINDING WAS NOT UNSETTLED: squadmates is printed on the TACTICS class feature itself ('when you drill, you can instruct a total number of allies equal to 2 + your Intelligence modifier … These allies are your squadmates'), and the dedication grants that feature by name and demands Intelligence +2, so no ruling was needed. Both round-trips fixed too — rebuildBuildFromCharacter and transfer.ts import each gated on the CLASS alone, so a dedicated character's folio was emptied on every round-trip and an imported one was 'accounted for' then fed to nobody. Also closed a pre-existing drift for REAL commanders: the builder capped the picker at the bare formula while the engine applied the counter mods, so a commander with Tactical Expansion could hold seven and was offered five; capacity and tier now come from two shared helpers. The record's note keeps its banner clause (30-foot tactics aura, no Will bonus against fear), which nothing else says. test/commander-via-dedication.test.ts (12).
